newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks mixed but Hong Kong hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks mixed but Hong Kong hits record high.

text.p: Asian stocks were mixed on Wednesday, but Hong Kong's Hang Seng index set a record as investors were cheered by the outlook for property shares and interest rates.
The Hang Seng index closed up 137.38 points at 12,943.69, after hitting a record intra-day peak at 12,951.85.
"People are reasonably bullish on property and by extension to a certain extent banking," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts said investors also were expecting U.S. interest rates to remain steady after the Federal Reserve's meeting scheduled for Wednesday.
They said the U.S. long bond yield, which fell to an eight-month low on Tuesday, was pointing in the right direction.

"People have looked at the U.S. market, looked at the bond market," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings. "Basically there is no reason to sell it and Hong Kong, valuation wise, is certainly not overstretched."
Osborn said investors may start "questioning the fundamentals" if the index hits 13,400 to 13,600 points.
Tokyo stocks shed all of the gains accumulated on Tuesday, battered by profit-taking as well as intermittent selling bouts of futures.
The Nikkei 225 average lost 226.99 points, or 1.07 percent, ending at 20,979.44.
"Small-lot selling munched away gains and once in a while futures-linked selling would add downward pressure," Harushige Kobayashi, Yamaichi Securities deputy general manager, said.
Market sources said a heavy lid was curtailing any rise in the Nikkei average at the 21,300 level, and both cash and futures were disappointed by it.
"Trading was directionless, and today's fall was part of the ongoing consolidation," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
In Singapore shares ended firm despite profit-taking. The Straits Times Industrials Index ended at 2,146.48, up 18.63 points.
Australian shares were slightly firmer, with the benchmark All Ordinaries index 3.4 points higher at 2,346.9.

Korean stocks went through wide fluctuations before ending lower. The composite index provisionally ended down 5.22 points at 747.32. Brokers said hopes of state actions to boost investment supported the market in early afternoon.
Investors were consolidating in Jakarta as well. The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.56 points, or 0.26 percent, to close at 595.49 points. Brokers said the trend was likely to continue on Thursday.
At 1115 GMT, the dollar was trading at 111.33/43 yen and 1.5059/64 marks.
Gold prices rose in Hong Kong. Bullion ended at US$382.60/383.10 an ounce against New York's US$382.20/70 close on Tuesday.
Oil futures were also higher, with the SIMEX December contract for Brent crude at $23.02 per barrel, up 19 cents from London's Tuesday close on the International Petroleum Exchange.
